```{r}
#| label: load-packages-data
#| message: FALSE

library(shinydashboard)
library(haven)
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(ggthemes)
library(forcats)
library(tidymodels)
library(plotly)


school_safety <- read_sas("data/pu_ssocs18.sas7bdat")
original_school_safety <- read_sas("data/pu_ssocs18.sas7bdat")
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_family = "Atkinson Hyperlegible"))

```

```{r}
#| label: filter-data

# filter the data, create final dataset to use
school_safety <- school_safety |>
  select(
    SCHID, # Unique school identifier
    INCPOL18, # Total number of incidents reported to police
    FR_URBAN, # Urbanicity - Based on urban-centric location of school
    FR_SIZE, # Size of school
    C0110:C0186, # School Practices and Programs 
    C0600,
    C0604:C0610,
    C0190:C0192,
    C0204:C0218,
    C0610:C0650,
    C0661,
    C0667,
    C0266:C0277, # Teacher Training
  )

school_safety <- school_safety |>
  mutate_at(vars(starts_with("C")), ~ str_replace(., "2", "0")) |>
  mutate_at(vars(starts_with("C")), ~ str_replace(., "-1", "0")) |>
  mutate(
    across(starts_with("C"), as.numeric),
    resource_sum = 
           C0183 + C0181 + C0179 + C0186 + C0604 + C0606 + C0608 + C0190 + 
           C0192 + C0204 + C0206 + C0208 + C0210 + C0212 + C0214 + C0216 + 
           C0218 + C0266 + C0268 + C0265 + C0267 + C0269 + C0270 + C0272 + 
           C0278 + C0271 + C0273 + C0274 + C0276 + C0277 + C0610,
    FR_URBAN = as.factor(FR_URBAN)
  ) |>
  arrange(resource_sum) 

```

```{r}
#| label: linear-regressions-for-each-resource

# adds names of school resources and practice variables
name <- colnames(school_safety |>
  select(starts_with("C")))

# create a vector to store all the values of the r-squared coefficients
r_squared_values <- numeric()
slope <- numeric()

# calculate all the r_squared values for every resource
for (variable in name) {
  lm_model <- lm(school_safety$INCPOL18 ~ factor(school_safety[[variable]])
                 + school_safety$FR_SIZE
                )
  r_squared <- summary(lm_model)$r.squared
  tidy_slope <- tidy(lm_model)|>
    filter(term == "factor(school_safety[[variable]])1")
  slope_value <- tidy_slope$estimate
  slope <- c(slope, slope_value)
  r_squared_values <- c(r_squared_values, r_squared)
}

# assign all vectors to the resource regression data frame
resource_regressions <- data.frame(name = name, 
                                    slope = slope, 
                                    r_squared_val = r_squared_values
                                    )

```

# Home

## Column

```{r}
#| label: scatter plot resources v. incidents all schools
#| fig-alt: |
#|   The graph is a jittered scatter plot titled, “Effect of School Resources on
#|   Incidents Reported to Police.” The x axis is “Amount of School
#|   Resources (out of 30)” and the y axis is “Total Number of Incidents
#|   Reported to the Police.” The x-axis ranges from 0 to a little above 30, 
#|   and the y axis ranges from 0 to about 350. The points are clustered close 
#|   to the x axis, with most of the points being below 100 incidents reported 
#|   to police, though there are some outliers above this line. Most notably, 
#|   there is one point located at 29 resources and 325 incidents reported to 
#|   police. There are also more points clustered between 10 and 30 school 
#|   resources compared to below 10 and over 30 (the points above 30 are due 
#|   to the degree of variability that results from jittering the points). 
#|   There appears to be a slight positive trend, with incidents reported to 
#|   police increasing as amount of school resources increases, though it is 
#|   very slight and difficult to discern. The shape of the distribution is a 
#|   very slight left skew.

# all schools resources and incidents plot
school_safety |>
  ggplot(aes(x = resource_sum, y = INCPOL18)) +
  geom_jitter() +
  labs(
    title = "Effect of School Resources on Incidents Reported to Police", 
    x = "Amount of School Resources (out of 30)",
    y = "Total Number of Incidents Reported to the Police"
  ) 

```

## Column {.tabset}

```{r}
#| label: Bar-graph-comparing-incidents-to-school-size
#| title: Total Incidents Between School Size
#| fig-alt: |
#|    This graph is a bar plot titled "Average Incidents Per School Compared to
#|    School Size". The x axis is "School Size" with four categories, each with
#|    their own bar: "less than 300," "300 - 499," "500 - 999," and "greater 
#|    than or equal to 1000." The y axis is "Average Incidents Per School," 
#|    ranging from 0 to about 30. The furthest-left bar, the "less than 300" 
#|    bar, is solid from 0 to about 2.5. The second bar from the left, the 
#|    "300 - 499" bar, is solid from 0 to about 3. The third bar from the left, 
#|    the "500 - 999" bar, is solid from 0 to about 7. The furthest-right bar, 
#|    the "greater than or equal to 1000" bar is solid from 0 to about 27.

# plot avg incidents based on school size
school_safety |>
  group_by(FR_SIZE) |>
  summarize(average_incidents_per_school = mean(INCPOL18)) |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = as.factor(FR_SIZE),
      y = average_incidents_per_school,
      fill = as.factor(FR_SIZE)
    )
  ) + 
  geom_col() + 
  labs(
    title = "Average Incidents Per School Compared to School Size", 
    x = "School Size", 
    y = "Average Incidents Per School"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("< 300", "300 - 499", "500 - 999", ">= 1000")) + 
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 30), breaks = seq(0, 30, by = 5)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  scale_fill_colorblind()
```

```{r}
#| label: Bar-graph-comparing-incidents-to-urbanicity
#| title: Total Incidents Between Urbanicity
#| fig-alt: |
#|    This graph is a bar plot titled "Average Incidents Per School Compared to
#|    School Urbanicity". The x axis is "School Urbanicity" with four 
#|    categories, each with their own bar: "City," "Suburban," "Town," and 
#|    "Rural." The y axis is "Average Incidents Per School," ranging from 0 to 
#|    about 30. The furthest-left bar, the "City" bar, is solid from 0 to about 
#|    14. The second bar from the left, the "Suburban" bar, is solid from 0 to 
#|    about 13. The third bar from the left, the "Town" bar, is solid from 0 to 
#|    a little above 10. The furthest-right bar, the "Rural" bar is solid from 
#|    0 to about 7.

# plot avg incidents based on urbanicity
school_safety |>
  mutate(FR_URBAN = fct_relevel(FR_URBAN, "4", "3", "2", "1")) |>
  group_by(FR_URBAN) |>
  summarize(average_incidents_per_school = mean(INCPOL18)) |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = FR_URBAN, 
      y = average_incidents_per_school, 
      fill = FR_URBAN
    )
  ) + 
  geom_col() + 
  labs(
    title = "Average Incidents Per School Compared to School Urbanicity", 
    x = "School Urbanicity", 
    y = "Average Incidents Per School"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = rev(levels(school_safety$FR_URBAN)),
                   labels = c("Rural", "Town", "Suburban", "City")) + 
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 30), breaks = seq(0, 30, by = 5)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = rev(colorblind_pal()(length(unique(school_safety$FR_URBAN)))))
```

```{r}
#| label: interactive-plot
#| title: School Resources and Practices
#| fig-alt: |
#|   The graph is a bar plot titled, “School Resources and Practices Impact
#|   on Incidents Reported to Police.” The x axis is titled, "School Resources 
#|   and Practices" and contains the variable names of 91 school 
#|   resources/practices, while the y axis graphs "Slope." Each variable has 
#|   its own bar that visualizes its slope compared to the other 
#|   variables' slopes. Most of the variables have slopes between 0 and 8, 
#|   although there are 22 variables with negative slopes, and 12 variables 
#|   with slopes above 8. When the cursor of the computer is hovered over a 
#|   bar, the variable name and slope will appear. The four variables with the 
#|   most identifiably strong (positive or negative) slopes are C0110, with a
#|   slope of -3.367, C0153, with a slope of -3.769, C0604, with a slope of
#|   9.054, and C0646, with a slope of 9.357. The colors of the bars correlate 
#|   to the R-squared values of the variables, with a scale ranging from light 
#|   blue to dark blue visualizing this. Variables with the lowest R-squared 
#|   values are colored lighter blue, while variables with the highest 
#|   R-squared values are colored darker blue.

# plot regressions
plot_ly(
  data = resource_regressions, 
  x = ~name, 
  y = ~slope, 
  type = 'bar', 
  text = ~paste("Variable: ", name, "<br>Slope: ", slope),
  hoverinfo = 'text', 
  marker = list(color = ~r_squared_val, colorscale = 'Blues')) |>
  layout(
    title = "School Resources and Practices Impact on Incidents Reported to Police",
    xaxis = list(title = "School Resources and Practices"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Slope")
  )
```

# C0646: Legal Definitions

## Column

```{r}
#| label: Legal-Def-Vary-with-Incidents
#| fig-alt: |
#|   The graph is a bar plot titled, “Sworn Law Enforcement Officers 
#|   Participating in Providing Legal Definitions Versus Average Incidents 
#|   Reported to Police in Schools.” The x axis is “Presence of Sworn Law 
#|   Enforcement Officers Participating in Providing Legal Definitions” with 
#|   the left bar labeled “No” and the right bar labeled “Yes.” The y axis is 
#|   “Average Incidents Reported to the Police per School” and ranges from 0 to 
#|   about 25. The left bar, the “No” bar, is filled in to about 4, and the 
#|   right bar, the “Yes” bar, is filled in to about 18.

# make C0646 a factor
school_safety <- school_safety |>
  mutate(C0646 = as.factor(C0646))

# plot officer participating in providing legal def and avg incidents reported 
# to police
school_safety |>
  group_by(C0646) |>
  summarize(average_incidents_per_school = mean(INCPOL18)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = C0646, y = average_incidents_per_school, fill = C0646)) + 
  geom_col() + 
  labs(
    title = "Sworn Law Enforcement Officers Participating in Providing Legal Definitions \nVersus Average Incidents Reported to Police in Schools", 
    x = "Presence of Sworn Law Enforcement Officers Participating in Providing Legal Definitions",
    y = "Average Incidents Reported to the Police per School"
  ) + 
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("No", "Yes")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 25)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  scale_fill_colorblind()
```

## Column

```{r}
#| label: Law-Officers-Legal-Def-Vary-with-Urbanicity
#| title: Urbanicity
#| fig-alt: |
#|   The graph is a segmented horizontal bar plot titled, “Sworn Law 
#|   Enforcement Officers Participating in Providing Legal Definitions Versus 
#|   School Urbanicity.” The x axis is “Quantity of Schools” and ranges from 
#|   0.00 to 1.00. The y axis is "Presence of Sworn Law Enforcement Officers 
#|   Participating in Providing Legal Definitions," with one bar for "Yes" and 
#|   one bar for "No." Color is used in this plot to represent "School 
#|   Urbanicity," with one color representing "City," one representing 
#|   "Suburban," one representing "Town," and one representing "Rural." The 
#|   "Yes" bar shows the breakdown of City, Suburban, Town, and Rural schools 
#|   with sworn law enforcement officers participating in providing legal 
#|   definitions, while the "No" bar shows the breakdown of schools that do 
#|   not have these officers participating. For the "Yes" bar, the "Rural" 
#|   portion of the bar goes from 0.00 to about 0.22, the "Town" portion goes 
#|   from about 0.22 to about 0.37, the "Suburban" portion goes from about 0.37 
#|   to about 0.78, and the "City" portion goes from about 0.78 to 1.00. For 
#|   the "No" bar, the "Rural" portion of the bar goes from 0.00 to about 0.24, 
#|   the "Town" portion goes from about 0.24 to about 0.35, the "Suburban" 
#|   portion goes from about 0.35 to about 0.70, and the "City" portion goes 
#|   from about 0.70 to 1.00.


#urbanicity graph
school_safety |>
  mutate(FR_URBAN = FR_URBAN, "Rural", "Town", "Suburban", "City") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = C0646, fill = as.factor(FR_URBAN))) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(
    title = "Sworn Law Enforcement Officers Participating in Providing Legal Definitions \nVersus School Urbanicity",
    fill = "School Urbanicity",
    x = "Presence of Sworn Law Enforcement Officers \nParticipating in Providing Legal Definitions",
    y = "Quantity of Schools",
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("No", "Yes")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  scale_fill_colorblind(labels = c("City", "Suburban", "Town", "Rural")) +
  coord_flip() +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE))

```
